pairs.question: Fortasse tu huc vocatus es ad prandium, ille qui vocavit nullus venit?
pairs.derivation: Daemones' full yes/no question kept verbatim; Plesidippus answers with the single affirming word Admodum ("just so"). No framing to cut; only terminal punctuation normalized.

pairs.question: Num medicus, quaeso, es?
pairs.answer: Immo edepol una littera plus sum quam medicus.
pairs.derivation: Gripus' question (num ... es?) and Labrax's direct reply, a punning "no" (medicus plus one letter = mendicus). Speech labels G./LABR. dropped; quaeso is part of the utterance, not a speech tag, so kept. Answer ends at the full stop before the next line's wordplay.

pairs.question: Quid perdidisti?
pairs.answer: Vidulum cum auro atque argento multo.
pairs.derivation: Gripus asks what Labrax lost; Labrax answers directly. Speaker labels GRIP./LABR. stripped. The following Gripus line (Ecquid meministi...) is a fresh question, not part of this answer.

pairs.question: In eo ensiculo litterarum quid est?
pairs.derivation: Daemones asks what letters are on the little sword; Palaestra answers. The imperative speech-framing 'Dice dum,' is dropped as a speech tag; the interrogative sentence is kept verbatim. First word capitalized after dropping the preceding tag.

pairs.question: In ensiculo quid nomen est paternum?
pairs.derivation: Daemones asks the father's name on the sword; Palaestra answers with the name. The imperative framing 'dic,' is dropped as a speech tag; the interrogative is kept verbatim, first word capitalized.
